Paperwork and rules, New Jersey

Before a roofer climbs the ladder: paperwork in New Jersey

Contractor registration, written contracts, roofing paperwork and storm claims, with the town offices to ask, as New Jersey's own pages laid them out on 1 November 2026. It is a reader's summary and not legal advice.

On this page

What a state registration number doesInsurance on file and the March renewalWhat goes into a written contractWhere roofing stands on permitsThe code edition a new roof answers toThe three-day cancellation rule, and its limitsStorm claims, step by stepWhom to ask in each town

What a state registration number does

The state's Division of Consumer Affairs runs registration for home improvement contractors, and its FAQ calls it mandatory: a business that makes or sells home improvements needs a registration number before it does the work. The number has to appear on ads, business cards, commercial vehicles and business documents, and each registration is renewed annually, before March 31.

According to the FAQ, state registration replaces any municipal licensing of these contractors, and since 1 January 2006 a town cannot issue a construction permit to a contractor who is required to register and has not. Checking is done online, through the Business Search on the Division's verification site. Roofing is not named as a trade in the FAQ, so the plain step is to ask for the number and look it up. Some people are exempt, such as someone working on a home they or a family member own.

Where the facts come from (3)
  1. NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, Home Improvement Contractor Registration FAQ
  2. NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, License Verification System
  3. Cornell LII, N.J.A.C. 13:45A-17.3, Registration required

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Insurance on file and the March renewal

Per the same FAQ, a registered contractor files proof of commercial general liability coverage with a $500,000-per-occurrence minimum, written in the contractor's own name. NJAC 13:45A-17.5 repeats the $500,000 floor and runs registration periods from 1 April through 31 March. A homeowner can ask to see the certificate before work begins.

Where the facts come from (2)
  1. NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, Home Improvement Contractor Registration FAQ
  2. Cornell LII, N.J.A.C. 13:45A-17.5, Initial and renewal applications

Checked 1 Nov 2026

What goes into a written contract

Home improvement work priced above $500 needs a written contract under NJAC 13:45A-16.2, signed by every party, with any later change put in writing as well. The rule's list of contents: the seller's legal name and business address; what the work is and the main products and materials; the full price including finance charges; start and finish dates or a time period; and anything the seller promises about the products, materials or labor. When someone besides the seller will act as general contractor, that name and address go in too.

The same rule has two lines worth reading twice. A seller may not ask a buyer to sign a completion certificate, or to make the last payment, until the job is done as the contract describes it. Work also cannot start until the seller has confirmed that the required permits were issued. The rule as read sets no limit on deposits.

Where the facts come from (1)
  1. Cornell LII, N.J.A.C. 13:45A-16.2, Home improvement contract requirements

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Where roofing stands on permits

The state's ordinary-maintenance alert, effective 5 March 2018, covers detached houses with one or two families. On such a house it counts any amount of re-covering or repair of existing roof covering, a full replacement included, as ordinary maintenance. Exterior gutters and leaders are on the list, and so is liquid-applied lining inside an existing chimney. Under NJAC 5:23-2.7, ordinary maintenance can proceed without a permit application or any notice to the construction official.

The alert also stresses that ordinary maintenance is no excuse for skipping the code. The Spring 2025 construction code newsletter treats reroofing as ordinary maintenance too, with a solar wrinkle: an electrical permit is required only when panel rails come off and grounding or bonding is compromised. Since the alert is written for detached homes with one or two families, anything attached or larger goes to the town office.

Where the facts come from (3)
  1. NJ Division of Codes and Standards, Ordinary Maintenance and Minor Work alert (5 Mar 2018)
  2. Cornell LII, N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, Ordinary maintenance
  3. NJ Department of Community Affairs, Construction Code Communicator, Spring 2025 (Solar and Reroofing)

Checked 1 Nov 2026

The code edition a new roof answers to

The state's codes page lists 17 August 2026 as the adoption date for the New Jersey editions of the 2024 International Building Code and International Residential Code. On ice, bulletin 07-3 (revised June 2015) requires an ice barrier where the daily January average temperature runs 25 degrees or colder, and its New Jersey entry is Sussex County. Teterboro's January average is 32.8 degrees, which is above that line.

The bulletin was written before the 2024 edition, so ask the town office whether anything has changed and whether it applies to a specific roof. The bulletin also exempts detached accessory structures with no conditioned floor area.

Where the facts come from (3)
  1. NJ Division of Codes and Standards, current model codes under the Uniform Construction Code
  2. NJ Division of Codes and Standards, Bulletin 07-3, Ice Dam Membrane/Ice Barrier (rev. June 2015)
  3. NOAA NCEI, 1991-2020 monthly climate normals, Teterboro Airport, NJ (station USW00094741)

Checked 1 Nov 2026

The three-day cancellation rule, and its limits

A federal rule, the FTC's Cooling-Off Rule, allows three business days to cancel certain purchases made in the buyer's own home. According to the FTC page, exceptions include emergencies and a visit the buyer requested in order to get repairs done, and sales under $25 are left out. A roof sale that starts with a homeowner phoning a roofer may fall under an exception, so the written contract is the document to read for any right to cancel.

Where the facts come from (1)
  1. Federal Trade Commission, Buyer's Remorse: The FTC's Cooling-Off Rule May Help

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Storm claims, step by step

New Jersey's Department of Banking and Insurance guide to storm claims asks homeowners to report the loss promptly, make temporary repairs and keep the receipts, and photograph damaged property before disposing of it. It also states that the homeowner chooses the contractor, with no obligation to take the insurance company's suggestion. The department's consumer hotline, listed in the guide, is 1-800-446-7467, open 8:30 to 5 on weekdays.

Where the facts come from (1)
  1. NJ Department of Banking and Insurance, Insurance claims after a storm

Checked 1 Nov 2026

What happens to your details, in a letter

This letter walks through what becomes of the details that come from a visit to qualitynortharlingtonroofing.com or from a call to the number shown there. The business behind it is Quality North Arlington Roofing, 70 Ridge Rd, North Arlington, NJ 07031, which puts homeowners and landlords in touch with a local roofing contractor by phone.

Who you are dealing withQuality North Arlington Roofing connects people who need roof work in North Arlington, Kearny, Lyndhurst or Belleville, New Jersey, with a local contractor. It does no roofing itself. The contractor who answers the call does the work, under its own agreement with the homeowner or landlord.

What a visit leaves behindWhoever hosts the pages keeps routine logs: an IP address, the browser and device in use, which pages were opened and when. Analytics tools may also count visits, taps on the phone number and where a call came from, using cookies or similar technology. Nothing on the pages asks a visitor to type anything, so a name or street address reaches the business only if a caller speaks it.

What happens on a callThe phone number shown on the pages runs through a call-tracking service. That service logs the caller's number, when the call happened, how long it lasted and which page or source brought the caller there. Calls are recorded only after a spoken notice, given at the start, says so. Whatever a caller mentions, from a name or street address to how the roof looks, becomes part of the call record.

Who gets the detailsThe contractor who answers is told what the caller says, enough to set up a visit. The call-tracking service, the analytics tools and the web host handle details on the way through. None of it is posted publicly or sold.

Cookies and browser signalsCookies can be blocked in the browser settings by anyone who wants less tracking. A Global Privacy Control signal sent by the browser is treated as a request that details not be sold or shared, and the pages behave the same either way.

Asking about a callTo find out what is held about a call, or to have it deleted, phone the number on the pages and ask. An answer comes within 45 days.

ChildrenThese pages are meant for adults who own or look after property, and nobody under 16 is their audience. The business does not seek details from children.

Changes to this letterIf the wording is revised, the updated version takes this one's place at /privacy/ under a new date.

Reaching the business about privacyFor a privacy question, call us and say so at the start.

Shingles, slate, metal and membranes

Roof materials, one covering at a time

A plain guide to the coverings found on roofs in North Arlington, Kearny, Lyndhurst and Belleville, drawn from federal agencies, the National Park Service and the asphalt roofing trade group. It describes what those pages say, not what any one roofer installs.

Asphalt shingles, the common covering

The National Park Service's roofing brief notes that asphalt shingles date from the 1890s and are common substitutes for wood, slate and tile. FEMA's fact sheet on asphalt shingles in high-wind regions asks for a starter strip at the eave, six nails per shingle there, roofing nails rather than staples, and underlayment every time, with a check that the tabs have sealed after the sun has warmed them.

The Department of Energy's cool-roof page says to choose light or cool-colored granules on asphalt shingles, and advises against field-coating existing shingles.

Where the facts come from (3)
  1. National Park Service, Preservation Brief 4: Roofing for Historic Buildings
  2. FEMA, Technical Fact Sheet No. 7.3, Asphalt Shingle Roofing for High-Wind Regions (copy hosted by the City of Goose Creek, SC)
  3. U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver: Cool roofs

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Slate and clay tile: heavy and brittle

The Park Service brief says top-grade slate with good flashing will last 40 to 60 years with minimal maintenance, and that soft slates erode and delaminate. Winter ice and ice dams are a major cause of breakage. Slate and tile cannot support much weight, so the brief advises against walking on them and suggests a ladder hung over the ridge or planks spanned across the roof.

Tiles crack when struck by branches or by foot traffic, and under-fired tiles craze and spall in freeze and thaw. The Department of Energy lists slate as usually not a cool roofing material.

Where the facts come from (2)
  1. National Park Service, Preservation Brief 4: Roofing for Historic Buildings
  2. U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver: Cool roofs

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Wood shingles and shakes

According to the Park Service brief, wood shingle faces erode from rain and ultraviolet light, and prolonged moisture lets moss or fungi grow, which leads to rot. Shingles wider than about 6 inches tend to split when walked on. The brief asks for inspection at least twice a year.

The Department of Energy describes wood shingles and shakes as naturally cool-colored.

Where the facts come from (2)
  1. National Park Service, Preservation Brief 4: Roofing for Historic Buildings
  2. U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver: Cool roofs

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Metal: pitting, streaks and mismatched metals

The Park Service brief lists what goes wrong with sheet metal: pitting and streaking from pollutants, galvanic corrosion where dissimilar metals touch, rust once an iron coating is worn, and fatigue at joints and protrusions. A galvanized coating protects iron only while it is intact.

On metal shingles and tiles, the Department of Energy recommends a light or cool paint applied at the factory, calls unpainted metal a poor choice, and says oven-baked factory paint holds up better than paint applied in the field.

Where the facts come from (2)
  1. National Park Service, Preservation Brief 4: Roofing for Historic Buildings
  2. U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver: Cool roofs

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Flat roof coverings

In the Department of Energy's terms, a roof pitched at 2:12 or flatter is low-slope. Its usual coverings include spray polyurethane foam, modified bitumen, built-up roofs and single-ply membranes, each with its own reflective options and each installed differently.

The Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association's page on ponding water gives 1/4 inch of fall per foot as the minimum slope, and counts water that is still standing after 48 hours as ponding. It names drains and scuppers as the exits and notes that freeze and thaw can scrub a membrane where water sits.

Where the facts come from (2)
  1. U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver: Cool roofs
  2. Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association, Ponding water basics

Checked 1 Nov 2026

The layer under the layer

The Department of Energy's repair brief describes underlayment as one layer of 30-pound felt with a 2-inch overlap, or two layers of 15-pound felt. FEMA's fact sheet says to use underlayment in every case.

The Building America guide to ice dam prevention adds self-adhering membranes around eaves, valleys, dormers and chimney penetrations, the spots where water is most likely to be pushed under a covering.

Where the facts come from (3)
  1. U.S. Department of Energy, Repairing Roofs and Ceilings technical brief
  2. FEMA, Technical Fact Sheet No. 7.3, Asphalt Shingle Roofing for High-Wind Regions (copy hosted by the City of Goose Creek, SC)
  3. Building America Solution Center (PNNL), Construct roofs and attics for ice dam prevention

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Light roofs, dark roofs and a cold winter

According to the Department of Energy, the surface of a standard roof can pass 150 degrees on a sunny summer afternoon, while a reflective roof stays more than 50 degrees cooler. Winter reverses part of the trade: a cool roof absorbs less sunlight and can add to heating needs, so in colder climates the energy cost may rise if that penalty outweighs the cooling savings. The page adds that cool roofs may be more prone to condensation than dark ones in cold climates, which proper design can prevent.

Teterboro Airport's normals run from a July average high of 87.0 degrees to a January average low of 25.7, so both seasons count here. The DOE page says a cool roof does not necessarily cost more on a new or replacement roof.

Where the facts come from (2)
  1. U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver: Cool roofs
  2. NOAA NCEI, 1991-2020 monthly climate normals, Teterboro Airport, NJ (station USW00094741)

Checked 1 Nov 2026

Choosing between two materials

A roofer can compare what two coverings would mean for a particular house: the weight on the frame, the pitch, the flashing details and the layers underneath. Start with roof replacement for a full job or flat roofs for a low-slope section, then call us and ask which covering suits the house.

Where the Rain Goes on a Roof: From the Ridge to the Gutter to the Ground

On 1 and 2 September 2021, a rain gauge in North Arlington collected 9.02 inches. Here is the path that water takes across a roof, layer by layer and joint by joint, and the places where it leaves the path.

A nine-inch nightThe stack under the shinglesEdges, where the water leavesMetal at the jointsWhen the roof is almost flatGutters, downspouts and the groundWhich sign on your roof is worth a call?The route of a raindrop, stage by stage

A nine-inch night

Ida's remnants dropped 9.02 inches on the New Jersey Weather and Climate Network's North Arlington gauge between 1 and 2 September 2021, with most of that falling in roughly six hours. Over the same two days Newark Airport logged 8.44 inches, and in Lyndhurst the single hour ending 9:30 PM brought 3.58.

Rutgers' water resources program supplies a way to picture it: an 800-square-foot roof collects about 500 gallons for every inch of rain. Scale that to 9.02 inches and the answer lands near 4,500 gallons, which is simple multiplication rather than a measurement. It still shows how much a roof handles on a bad night.

The route of a raindrop, stage by stage

  1. Shingle surface

    Sheds most of the water

    First sign of trouble: grit in the downspouts, curled edges

  2. Underlayment

    Backs up the shingles

    First sign of trouble: a stain inside with no visible hole

  3. Flashing

    Seals chimneys, walls and vents

    First sign of trouble: a stain beside the chimney or wall

  4. Valley

    Carries the water of two slopes

    First sign of trouble: a stain below the line where slopes meet

  5. Eave

    Hands water to the gutter

    First sign of trouble: ice at the edge, a stained soffit

  6. Gutter

    Collects the runoff

    First sign of trouble: overflow in an ordinary rain

  7. Downspout

    Ends the trip at the ground

    First sign of trouble: wet foundation or driveway at its foot

The stack under the shingles

Shingles are the visible layer, and they turn away most of the water. Beneath them lies underlayment, a sheet meant to resist water if any gets past, and below that the deck of boards or plywood that carries everything. FEMA's technical fact sheet on shingles for high-wind regions asks for underlayment under every installation.

The Department of Energy's repair brief gives two typical builds: a single layer of 30-pound felt lapped 2 inches, or in place of that two 15-pound layers. The overlaps do a simple job. Water that slips past one layer meets the next and keeps running downhill.

Edges, where the water leaves

The eave is where the roof passes its water to the gutter. FEMA's fact sheet calls for a starter strip along the eave and six nails per shingle there, roofing nails rather than staples. A weak edge is where wind lifts the first course and lets rain underneath.

Winter turns the eave into the place where ice builds. As UMass's building-science group describes it, snow melts over the heated part of the roof, then freezes again once it reaches the cold overhang, and the water that backs up behind that ice finds its way under the shingles. The Building America guide recommends self-adhering membranes around eaves, valleys, dormers and chimney penetrations.

Metal at the joints

Wherever a roof meets something else, metal takes over. Along a wall, the Building Science Corporation's flashing details show step flashing woven in with the shingles and kick-out flashing at the bottom that steers water away from the wall. At a chimney, counterflashing is set into the mortar joints and laps over the base flashing.

The National Park Service's roofing brief calls a failure in the flashing system usually a major reason roofs deteriorate, and the asphalt roofing trade group's post-Sandy guide names flashings as the most vulnerable part of a roof. A leak beside a chimney or a wall is worth tracing to the joint before anyone replaces a shingle.

When the roof is almost flat

Low-slope roofs drain slowly by design; the Department of Energy draws the line at a pitch no steeper than 2:12. The Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association says water still sitting there 48 hours after the rain is ponding, gives 1/4 inch of fall per foot as the minimum slope, and points to drains and scuppers as the exits. Freeze and thaw can scrub a membrane where water sits.

The usual coverings are single-ply sheets, built-up layers and modified bitumen, each installed differently. A puddle still there two days after the rain is a fair question to put to a roofer.

Gutters, downspouts and the ground

A gutter collects what the roof sheds, and a downspout carries it to the ground. The National Park Service's brief ties a roof's success to frequent cleaning and repair of the gutter system, because debris blocks the flow and sends water backing up beneath the roofing. The Rutgers rain barrel page suggests sending downspouts to a spot where water can soak in, and the EPA's page on redirecting them cautions that it is not right for every property and that local regulations apply.

Where the water lands matters too. Bergen County's hazard plan puts about 21 percent of North Arlington's land in the mapped floodplain, and the CDC's guidance for flooded homes says rainwater from gutters or the roof needs to drain away from the house.

Which sign on your roof is worth a call?

Stains on a ceiling, grit in the downspouts, a gap beside the chimney or water that stays on a flat section are the usual first signs. A stain that grows with every rain points to roof repair, and water on the ground by the wall points to gutters and downspouts.

Next step: call us and say which sign you are seeing and where; the street address, and a yard photo if you took one, move things along.

Belleville, NJ

Roofing in Belleville, NJ: Third River Streets and Older Roofs

Contact details

Several Belleville neighborhoods flood from the Third River, according to the township itself, so it pays to separate roof water from ground water early. For a stain, a spilling gutter or wind damage, start with storm damage or roof repair, then call us and tell the roofer which part of the roof is involved.

About the homes

The middle Belleville home was built in 1951, with a margin of 3 years, among 15,104 homes in the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate for the township. Detached houses are 6,375 of them, 42.2 percent; two-unit buildings number 3,040 and buildings with three or four units 1,198. Of 14,356 occupied homes, 6,326 are rented, or 44.1 percent. Detached houses and two-family buildings mix on the same streets, so a single block can hold one-household roofs and two-household roofs.

Around town

Across the river from Ridge Road

The township hall is at 152 Washington Avenue. Belleville borders Bloomfield, Newark, Nutley, Lyndhurst, North Arlington and Kearny, and the Route 7 bridge over the Passaic River connects it with North Arlington.

What neighbors ask

What is the Third River flooding in Belleville?

A township notice from 6 December 2021 says neighborhoods around Fairway Avenue, Suzanne Court, Carolyn Road, Dorothea Terrace and the Bridgebrook condominiums routinely flood from the Third River, and that the mayor asked state officials for help.

What did Belleville tell residents after Ida?

The township's 8 September 2021 update told residents to contact their insurance company and called photos and videos extremely helpful, while the Department of Public Works was removing damaged property. Dated photos of roof and ceiling damage serve the same purpose.

Who can call about a Belleville roof?

Anyone who owns or manages a building here can call us; the address, the roof's age and a short description of what shows from the ground are enough to start. Before any roofer, a renter talks to the landlord or property manager. For danger of any kind, 911 comes ahead of everything.

Contact details

What goes wrong here

Where Belleville roofs and rain collide

Streets near the Third River.

Fairway Avenue, Suzanne Court, Carolyn Road, Dorothea Terrace and the Bridgebrook condominiums routinely flood from the Third River, according to a township notice from December 2021. A downspout that ends near a foundation on those streets adds to the problem; see gutters and downspouts.

After-storm records.

The township's September 2021 Ida update told residents to contact their insurers and called photographs and videos extremely helpful. That is the same record a roofer and an insurer both ask for; see storm damage.

Mixed blocks.

Detached houses are 42 percent of Belleville's homes and buildings with two, three or four units about 28 percent, so a roofer arriving on a block may see both kinds.

Roofing in Kearny, NJ: Two- and Three-Family Roofs

Contact details

Kearny's housing is dense and layered: more than four in ten homes sit in two-, three- or four-unit buildings, so one roof often covers several households. For a stain, a loose gutter or a lifted run of shingles, start with roof repair or gutters and downspouts, then call us with the address and what you can see.

About the homes

In the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate, Kearny's median home, among 15,367, dates from 1951, give or take 3 years. Detached houses number 4,618, attached houses 853, two-unit buildings 4,070 and buildings with three or four units 2,427. Rented homes account for 8,418 of the 14,751 occupied ones, or 57.1 percent, so plenty of Kearny households will begin with a message to the landlord or property manager.

Around town

Kearny's edge along Route 7

North Arlington lies along Kearny's northern edge, where the Belleville Turnpike (Route 7) runs. Town Hall is at 402 Kearny Ave, and the construction code enforcement page points its map to the annex at 410 Kearny Ave. Of the other three towns here, Belleville and Lyndhurst also share a border with Kearny.

What neighbors ask

What kinds of buildings does Kearny have?

Out of 15,367 homes in the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate, 4,618 are detached houses, 853 attached, 4,070 two-unit buildings and 2,427 have three or four units. The median home was built in 1951, give or take 3 years, which is worth remembering when a roof's age comes up.

Does Kearny have a downspout rule?

Kearny's stormwater page lists an illicit-connection ordinance but says nothing about roof leaders or downspouts. Where a downspout may drain is a question for the town office, and it is worth settling before anyone redirects one.

Who can call about a Kearny roof?

If you own the building, or manage it for an owner, call us with the address, the roof's age and what you can see from the ground. A renter's first move is a message to the landlord or property manager. Danger comes before any of that: dial 911.

Contact details

What goes wrong here

Trouble spots on a Kearny roof

One roof, several households.

In a two-, three- or four-unit building, a stain in one flat may come from a roof section over another. A dated photo of the stain, passed to the landlord or property manager, helps the roofer find the right slope.

Gutters and where the water ends up.

Rutgers' rule of thumb, 500 gallons off 800 square feet of roof for each inch of rain, is a lot of water for a side yard, so it is worth checking where each downspout ends. Kearny's stormwater page lists an illicit-connection ordinance but nothing on roof leaders, so ask the town. See gutters and downspouts.

Flat sections.

A flat roof over a rear addition or a porch drains slowly by design, and water still standing two days after a rain is the sign to look; see flat roofs.

Roofing in Lyndhurst, NJ: Meadowlands Water and Roof Runoff

Contact details

About half of Lyndhurst's land lies in the mapped floodplain, which makes it worth tracing where roof water goes after it leaves the roof. For a spilling gutter or a wet basement wall, start with gutters and downspouts; for a stain on the ceiling, roof repair. Next step: call us and say which wall or gutter is wet.

About the homes

The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate counts 9,704 homes in Lyndhurst township, with a median year built of 1956 (give or take 3 years). Detached houses make up 4,063 of them, 41.9 percent, two-unit buildings 2,884 and buildings with three or four units 600. Of 9,208 occupied homes, 3,718 are rented, or 40.4 percent, the lowest renter share among North Arlington, Kearny, Lyndhurst and Belleville.

Around town

Between the Passaic and the Meadowlands

The township hall is at 367 Valley Brook Ave. The Passaic River forms Lyndhurst's western border, and the eastern part is uninhabited Meadowlands wetland. Lyndhurst touches North Arlington, Kearny and Belleville, as well as Rutherford, Nutley, Secaucus and Clifton.

What neighbors ask

How much of Lyndhurst sits in the floodplain?

Bergen County's 2026 hazard plan counts 1,618.43 of the township's 3,178.68 acres, 50.92 percent, in the 1 percent annual-chance floodplain, and notes that parts of Lyndhurst are affected by coastal flooding from Hackensack River surges.

How hard did Ida rain on Lyndhurst?

The New Jersey Weather and Climate Network logged 3.58 inches in Lyndhurst in the single hour ending 9:30 PM, during Ida's passage on 1 and 2 September 2021. North Arlington's station recorded 9.02 inches over the two days, and Newark Airport 8.44.

Who can call about a Lyndhurst roof?

Property owners and landlords can call us with the address, the roof's age and what shows from the ground. A renter asks the landlord or property manager before anything else. If something feels dangerous, 911 comes first.

Contact details

What goes wrong here

Roof trouble that follows water in Lyndhurst

Runoff on wet ground.

Bergen County's hazard plan puts 1,618.43 of Lyndhurst's 3,178.68 acres, 50.92 percent, in the mapped 1 percent annual-chance floodplain. A downspout that empties beside a foundation adds to ground that is already wet; see gutters and downspouts.

Short, hard rain.

During Ida, Lyndhurst recorded 3.58 inches in the single hour ending 9:30 PM. An hour like that tests every valley, drain and gutter corner on the roof.

Ice at the eaves.

The January normals at Teterboro Airport show about 16 days that dip below freezing overnight and climb above it by afternoon; see ice dams.

North Arlington, NJ

Roofing in North Arlington, NJ: Older Roofs on Older Houses

Contact details

With a median build year of 1954, the houses around Ridge Road are old enough that the roof's own history is worth asking about. If a stain, a lifted shingle or a loose gutter brought you here, roof repair is the place to start, and roof inspection covers the roof nobody has looked at in years. Dial us and ask when someone can look.

About the homes

The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate counts about 6,900 homes in North Arlington, give or take 380, with a median year built of 1954 (margin 2 years). By its year-built ranges, 2,228 homes date from the 1950s, 1,177 from the 1940s and 1,366 from 1939 or earlier, and only 262 were built in 2010 or later. Two-unit buildings number 1,838 and buildings with three or four units 871, and 55.6 percent of occupied homes are rented. For a roof, that adds up to a lot of buildings with several households under one roofline, and a lot of roofs worth a question about how many layers sit beneath the top one.

Around town

Around Ridge Road

Borough Hall is at 214 Ridge Road, and the business address, 70 Ridge Rd, is on the same road. North Arlington is the southernmost municipality in Bergen County. Its neighbors are Lyndhurst, Kearny to the south along the Belleville Turnpike (Route 7), and Belleville across the Passaic River by way of the Route 7 bridge.

What neighbors ask

How old are the houses under North Arlington's roofs?

By the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate the median home was built in 1954, give or take 2 years, and about 69 percent date from 1959 or earlier. A house's age is not its roof's age, since roofs get replaced, so the useful question for a roofer is how many layers are up there.

What did Ida do in North Arlington?

The remnants of Ida left 9.02 inches of rain at the North Arlington station on 1 and 2 September 2021, mostly in about six hours, according to the New Jersey Weather and Climate Network. Newark Airport logged 8.44 inches. Dated photos help with any later talk about storm damage.

Who can call about a North Arlington roof?

Homeowners and landlords can dial us and give the street address, what shows from the ground and the roof's age. Renters, your first call goes to the landlord or property manager. Anything dangerous goes to 911 before any call to a roofer.

Contact details

What goes wrong here

Where older roofs here fail first

Layers on layers.

A house built around 1954 has had time to collect more than one roof. Ask how many layers are up there and how many will come off, since the answer shapes the quote.

Metal at the joints.

About 2,500 homes date from before 1950, and the flashing at chimneys and walls is worth a look on houses that old. The National Park Service's roofing brief names failed flashing as usually a major cause of roof deterioration; see chimney and flashing.

Water at the foundation.

About 21 percent of the borough's land is in the mapped floodplain, and Ida left 9.02 inches at the station in 2021. Where a downspout lands matters; see gutters and downspouts.

A stain nobody mentions.

More than half of the occupied homes here are rented, 55.6 percent, and a stain can go unreported when the person who sees it is not the person who owns the roof. Renters reach the landlord or property manager first.

Gaps, stains and loose metal around the brick

Chimney and Flashing in North Arlington, NJ

Is there a brown mark on the wall by the chimney, or a gap where the brick meets the shingles? Call us and say where the mark shows and what the chimney is made of, and the roofer can plan a look at the flashing and the mortar.

Contact detailsPairs with ice dams

When it cannot wait

A stain that follows the chimney up

A leak that tracks a chimney, a wall or a vent pipe can come from the metal sealing the joint rather than from the shingles around it. The National Park Service's roofing brief names failed flashing as usually a major cause of roof deterioration.

A ceiling stain near the chimney after wind-driven rain, a gap you can see from the yard between brick and metal, or loose, lifted metal is reason to call us and book a look this week.

What the work involves

Two layers of metal at the chimney base

At a chimney the metal comes in two parts. Base flashing is tucked under the shingles and turns up the brick. Counterflashing is set into the mortar joints above it and laps down over the base. Rain that runs down the brick meets metal first and shingles second.

Along a wall the Building Science Corporation's flashing details show step flashing woven in with the shingles, and kick-out flashing at the bottom to steer water away from the wall.

Stop and get help first if

  • Smoke, a burning smell or soot is coming from the chimney or the walls around it: leave the house and call 911.
  • A brick or a chunk of the cap has dropped, or the stack leans: keep everyone from standing underneath, and leave the fireplace unlit.
  • Gas odor inside or near the chimney: get out, touch no switches, and dial PSE&G's gas line, 1-800-880-7734, or 911 from outside.
  • Someone wants to climb onto a steep roof to look at the chimney: do not. The base shows from the ground with binoculars, or from an upstairs window.

Close to home

The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 year-built ranges put 1,366 North Arlington homes at 1939 or earlier and 1,177 in the 1940s, about 2,500 homes before 1950, give or take roughly 400. Chimneys, counterflashing and mortar joints on those houses are as old as the houses, or have been rebuilt along the way.

Winter carries as much precipitation as summer at Teterboro Airport in the 1991-2020 normals: 4.10 inches in December and 4.09 in March, against 4.45 in July. A joint between brick and metal that leaks in August can leak again in December.

What moves the price

What a flashing quote is made of

A chimney's flashing job depends on the chimney: how wide it is, whether it sits mid-slope or at an edge, how many sides need metal, and whether the mortar joints that hold the counterflashing need repointing first. A small peaked saddle behind a wide chimney adds work.

The metal chosen, such as aluminum, galvanized steel or copper, changes the material cost. Repointing is masonry work, so it may be quoted separately or by a different trade.

Paperwork pointer

Chimney work and the state list

The state's maintenance alert names liquid-applied lining inside an existing chimney as ordinary maintenance. It does not mention repointing or masonry repair, so ask the town office about those; the rules page lists the office in each town.

Ponding, seams and low-slope roofs on older houses

Flat Roof Repair in North Arlington, NJ

Does water sit on the flat part of the roof for a day or more after the rain has ended? Call us and say where it collects, what the surface is made of and its age, and the roofer can arrange to see the seams and drains.

Contact detailsPairs with gutters and downspouts

When it cannot wait

Water that stays after the sky clears

A flat roof is meant to shed water slowly, not to keep it. The Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association calls it ponding when water is still there 48 hours after the rain stops, and it gives 1/4 inch of fall per foot as the minimum slope for drainage. Freeze and thaw can wear a membrane where water stays.

Standing puddles past that mark, a stain on the ceiling under the flat section, or a membrane that blisters, splits or lifts at an edge: any of them is enough to dial us and book a look this week.

What the work involves

Where a flat roof gives way first

Flat and low-slope sections, such as a rear addition, a porch or the top of a bay, fail at the same few places: the seams between sheets of membrane, the corners and edges, the spots where a pipe or a wall rises through, and the drain or scupper where water is supposed to leave.

Under the Department of Energy's definition, low-slope means a pitch no steeper than 2:12, and the usual coverings are single-ply membranes, built-up roofs and modified bitumen. Each is installed differently, so a seam repair on one is not the same job as on another.

Stop and get help first if

  • Water has stood on the flat section for days and the ceiling underneath is drooping: close that room off, and call 911 if the ceiling starts to come down.
  • The surface feels soft or springy underfoot: stay off the roof and keep others off it, since the deck below may be rotted.
  • Wires cross close to the parapet or the roof edge: stay off the roof, and phone the utility or 911 if one is sagging or sparking.
  • A ceiling light drips or buzzes after rain: leave the room, leave the switch alone, and call 911 from a dry spot.

Close to home

The borough's mix includes 329 attached houses, 1,838 two-unit buildings and 871 with three or four units, per the 2020-2024 Census estimate. Additions, porches and bays often carry a flat section, and a walk around the outside of the house shows whether yours does.

Teterboro's July normals pair an average high of 87.0 degrees with 1.5 days that reach an inch of rain. The Department of Energy says a standard roof surface can climb to 150 degrees or higher under afternoon sun, which is hard on a membrane that then has to take a summer downpour.

What moves the price

What drives the price of a flat roof job

A seam repair, a section replacement and a full re-cover are three different prices. The covering sets the base: single-ply sheets, built-up layers and modified bitumen each go on differently. After that come the drains and edges, the number of pipes and vents poking through, and whether wet insulation has to be pulled out. The Department of Energy's repair brief says soaked insulation has to be removed.

If water ponds, slope and drainage enter the conversation too, since the trade group ties standing water to slope, drains and scuppers.

Paperwork pointer

Paperwork on a flat section

The state's maintenance alert deals with detached homes holding one or two families, and a flat section often belongs to an attached house or a larger building. Whether a job needs a permit is the town office's call; the rules page names the office in each town.

Overflow, sagging runs and downspouts that dump

Gutters and Downspouts in North Arlington, NJ

Is water spilling over the edge of the gutter, or pooling beside the foundation after a heavy rain? Call us with where it spills, which downspout feeds the wet spot and whether the run sags, and the roofer can schedule a look at the run.

Contact detailsPairs with flat roofs

When it cannot wait

Water going over the edge instead of down

Three signs say a gutter job cannot wait for spring. Water slops over the front lip in a normal rain. A run has pulled away from the fascia, or a corner has opened up. Or a wet streak shows on the wall below the gutter, or the basement wall is damp after storms.

Each means roof water is going somewhere it was never meant to. Call us and ask for a look at the run, and name the downspout nearest the wet spot.

What the work involves

The parts of a gutter run

A run has four parts worth knowing by name. The gutter itself tilts slightly toward the outlet. Hangers hold it to the fascia board. The outlet drops into a downspout, and the downspout ends in an elbow or an extension that points water away from the wall.

The EPA's page on redirecting downspouts cautions that disconnecting one is not right for every property and that local regulations apply, so check before changing where one drains.

Stop and get help first if

  • A gutter, downspout or ladder is touching a power line: do not touch the metal, keep everyone clear, and call 911 or the utility.
  • Water is seeping into a basement with a panel or outlets nearby: do not step in it, leave the area, and call 911 if it keeps rising.
  • Heavy icicles or a loaded gutter are pulling away from the fascia: keep people, pets and cars out from beneath it, and do not knock the ice down from a ladder.
  • A ladder is the only way to reach the gutter: do not climb on frozen ground or with wet gloves, and leave the cleaning to a roofer.

Close to home

Rutgers Water Resources puts the yield of an 800-square-foot roof at about 500 gallons per inch of rain. Ida's 9.02 inches at the North Arlington station (1-2 September 2021) works out to roughly 4,500 gallons from that much roof, by simple multiplication rather than any published measurement.

The 2026 Bergen County hazard mitigation plan maps 344.85 of North Arlington's 1,619.78 acres, about 21 percent, in the 1 percent annual-chance floodplain. With so much low ground in the borough, it matters where a downspout empties.

No downspout rule turned up in North Arlington's borough pages, and Kearny's stormwater page mentions an illicit-connection ordinance but nothing about roof leaders. Before changing where a downspout empties, ask the town office.

What moves the price

How a gutter quote adds up

Length of run and number of corners come first. The material matters next: aluminum, steel and copper each carry a different price and a different set of edge details. Then come the downspout count, the height of the eave, whether the fascia boards behind are sound enough to hold new hangers, and whether the run is being cleaned, repaired, re-pitched or replaced.

A cleaning is the smallest job in the group. A replacement of a long run on a three-story house is the largest.

Paperwork pointer

Where downspouts may drain

The state's list of ordinary maintenance includes work on exterior gutters and leaders, whether repair, replacement or a brand-new installation, with no permit application. Whether a town limits where a downspout discharges is a separate question; the rules page lists the offices to ask.

Ice at the eaves with a damp ceiling or wall

Ice Dams on North Arlington Roofs

Is there a ridge of ice along the eaves, with a damp patch on the ceiling or the wall beneath? Call us with where the ice sits, how long it has been there and where the stain shows, and a roofer can come out to look at the eaves and the attic side.

Contact detailsPairs with chimney and flashing

When it cannot wait

Ice on the eave, water in the wall

An ice dam needs three things: snow on the roof, heat leaking up from the house, and a cold eave. Melt from the warm part of the roof refreezes at the edge, backs up behind the ice and finds its way under the shingles. UMass's building-science group says one or two inches of snow can be enough.

Once the water reaches a ceiling or wall, dial us and say where the ice sits along the eave. Insulation that has gotten damp needs a look before the next freeze.

What the work involves

The cure is usually in the attic

The lasting answer to an ice dam is rarely at the eave. UMass's building-science group points to air sealing, insulation and ventilation in the attic, and notes that heat cable does not address the cause and that gutters do not create the dam.

The Building America guide adds the roofing side: self-adhering membranes around eaves, valleys, dormers and chimney penetrations.

Stop and get help first if

  • Meltwater is coming through a ceiling fixture: leave the room, leave the switch alone, and call 911 from a dry spot.
  • Heavy icicles hang above an entry or a walk: block off the spot below, and leave them alone instead of knocking them down from a ladder.
  • The plan for the ice involves a ladder, a roof rake or a shovel on an icy roof: do not climb up, and keep anyone off the ground below the eave.
  • Inside, a ceiling bellies out or a wall runs with water: clear everyone from beneath it, and call 911 at the first sign of plaster or board coming down.

Close to home

Teterboro Airport's 1991-2020 normals average January at 32.8 degrees. In a typical January the low reaches 32 or colder on 23.6 days, and the high stays at 32 or colder on 7.7. The difference, about 16 days, is the freeze-at-night, thaw-by-afternoon stretch (derived by subtraction) that feeds an ice dam.

The National Weather Service's Newark almanacs for 1991-2020 give a mean January snowfall of 9.1 inches and February's at 10.1. Newark is the station those almanacs cover, so snow on one North Arlington street can differ, but UMass notes that an ice dam can form under as little as 1 to 2 inches.

What moves the price

What separates a thaw job from a winter job

Removing ice with care is labor by the hour, and the price follows the size of the dam and how far the ice reaches. The work that stops the next one is different: sealing air leaks at the attic floor, adding insulation, improving ventilation and, on a reroof, laying a self-adhering membrane along the eaves. Those are separate line items, and the first two may belong to a different trade from the roofer.

Ask who is quoting what.

Paperwork pointer

Ice barrier and the state code

The state's ice barrier bulletin of June 2015 applies its requirement where the January average falls to 25 degrees or colder; its New Jersey entry is Sussex County. Since the bulletin was issued before the 2024 edition was adopted, ask the town office what applies now. The rules page has the details and the offices: the local rules page.

A close look before a small problem grows

Roof Inspection in North Arlington, NJ

Is the roof so old that nobody remembers when it went on, or has a storm just passed over it? Call us with the address and the age of the house, and a roofer can set a time to look it over before anything leaks.

Contact detailsPairs with storm damage

When it cannot wait

Reasons to look before the next season

Plenty of roofs get looked at only when they leak. A walk around in autumn, ahead of the first freeze, or in spring after the thaw, catches a lifted flashing or a clogged valley while it is still a small job. The National Park Service's roofing brief asks for inspection at least twice a year and names flashing failure as usually a major cause of roof deterioration.

A house that has just changed hands, or a roof nobody has seen in a decade, is also a fair reason. Dial us and ask for a time; the address and the roof's age, if known, help.

What the work involves

What a roofer walks past, in order

From the ground, the roofer looks along the ridge and eaves, then at the gutters and the walls under the roofline. Up top, the work covers the field of shingles, the flashing at every chimney, wall and vent, the valleys and the way the edges are finished. In the attic, a flashlight shows the underside of the boards, the insulation and any dark trails left by water.

Ladder falls in the United States kill more than 100 people a year, NIOSH reports, which is reason enough to keep homeowner checks at ground level, with binoculars.

Stop and get help first if

  • A service cable has come loose from the house or lies on the roof edge: assume it is live, stay well back, and call 911 or the utility.
  • Someone is about to climb a ladder to look: do not set it near wires or on soft, sloping ground, and stay off it altogether when the surface is wet.
  • Smoke or a scorched smell comes from the attic or around the chimney: leave the house and call 911.
  • The attic floor feels spongy or the ceiling below is bowed: stay off the attic floor and keep others out of the room beneath.

Close to home

By the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 year-built ranges, about 89 percent of North Arlington's homes (6,157 of roughly 6,900) predate 1980, and 1,366 go back to 1939 or earlier. On a house of that vintage, ask the roofer to count the shingle layers and to look closely at the metal around the chimney.

The Teterboro Airport normals for 1991-2020 run from an average July high of 87.0 degrees down to a January average low of 25.7, a spread of about 61 degrees (derived by subtraction). Roofing materials expand and contract across that range every year, and that wear is what an inspection looks for.

What moves the price

What the price of a look depends on

A walk-through with a short written summary is a different job from a full report with photographs of each slope. The size of the roof, how steep it is, whether the attic can be reached and how many stories the roofer has to climb all change the time.

Questions worth asking: what the visit includes, whether photos come with it, and whether the price is credited if repair work follows.

Paperwork pointer

Who needs to know about an inspection

An inspection is a look, not work, so the paperwork questions begin only if repairs follow. For those, the rules page covers what the state exempts, what each town's office handles and how to check a contractor: before work begins.

Stains, curled shingles and wind damage nearby

Roof Repair in North Arlington, NJ

Is a ceiling stain spreading after each rain, or are shingles turning up in the yard? Call us, point to the spot and say when you first noticed it, and a roofer can arrange a time to come look.

Contact detailsPairs with roof replacement

When it cannot wait

When a damp spot starts spreading

A drip into a bucket during a dry week is a nuisance. Water that returns to the same place with every storm, a stain that has crossed its pencil line twice, or insulation that feels heavy and cold is another matter, because wet wood and wet insulation stay wet long after the sky clears.

The EPA's mold guide opens with the same advice: water problems need attention as soon as they turn up, and wet material needs drying all the way through. Any one of those three signs is enough to dial us and ask when a roofer can look; jot down the date of each stain first.

What the work involves

How one shingle comes out and another goes in

The row above is lifted just far enough to reach the nails holding the damaged shingle. Those nails are pulled, the old shingle slides out, and the new one slips in with its nails set in the nailing strip, where the next row will cover the heads. The upper tabs press back down, and the neighbors get a look, since a cracked shingle often has a cracked neighbor.

FEMA's technical fact sheet on asphalt shingles calls for roofing nails rather than staples, underlayment beneath, and a check that the tabs have sealed once the sun has warmed them.

Stop and get help first if

  • Water is running from a ceiling fixture or a wall plug: step out of the room, leave the switch alone, and call 911 from a dry spot.
  • Part of a ceiling has bellied downward and looks heavy: clear the room beneath it, and call 911 if the plaster or board begins to drop.
  • A wire lies across the roof, the yard or a tree branch: assume it is energized, keep about two pole spans (30 feet) between you and it, and dial 1-800-436-7734 for PSE&G, or 911 if anyone is close to it.
  • A relative or neighbor offers to climb up and look while the roof is wet, frosty or steep: talk them out of it, and call 911 only if someone has already fallen.

Close to home

The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 survey puts the middle North Arlington house at 1954, give or take 2 years, and roughly 69 percent of the borough's 6,900 or so homes went up in 1959 or before. Houses from that stretch may be wearing several layers of shingles, so ask how many are up there before anyone quotes a patch.

Teterboro Airport, the NOAA station about 6 miles away in the 1991-2020 normals, records July as its wettest month at 4.45 inches, with June and August each at 4.25. On average 1.5 July days deliver at least an inch of rain, the sort of downpour that finds a gap in a shingle course.

More than half of the occupied homes here are rented: 3,699 of 6,649, or 55.6 percent, with a margin of about 441 on the renter count, in the same Census estimate. Anyone renting who spots a stain contacts the landlord or property manager first.

What moves the price

What changes the number on a patch quote

How many shingles are damaged counts for less than how far the water got. A wet shingle is a short job; a soaked deck means boards cut out and replaced. Height and pitch change the setup, and so do the pieces nearby, such as a chimney, a vent pipe or a valley, each of which brings flashing to check.

A house already carrying two or three layers of old shingle gives the roofer more to work through. The Department of Energy's repair brief passes along a guide's line for the bigger question: past 10 percent of the old roof needing repair, price a new one beside the patch.

Paperwork pointer

Paperwork for a repair

A detached home with one or two families sits under a state list of ordinary maintenance, and patching the roof covering is on it, so no permit application is needed. Attached homes, larger buildings and each town's office are covered on the local rules page.

A new covering for older houses, layer by layer

Has the roof reached the point where each patch buys less time?

A new covering for older houses, layer by layer

Roof Replacement in North Arlington, NJ

Has the roof reached the point where each patch buys less time? Call us with its age, the number of layers you know of and where it has leaked, and the roofer can plan a visit to look over every slope.

Contact detailsPairs with roof repair

When it cannot wait

Signs the old roof is done

Shingles that curl at the edges, shed grit into the downspouts or crack when touched have reached the end. So has a roof with leaks in two or three places that keep coming back after patches. A sagging ridge line, or daylight showing through the boards in the attic, means the frame under the covering needs a look soon, not next season.

Seeing two or more of these is reason to dial us and ask when a roofer can come. A winter of waiting can turn a roof job into a roof, insulation and ceiling job.

What the work involves

A tear-off, from the top layer down

Replacement starts with the old shingles and nails coming off. The deck gets checked for soft or stained boards, and anything bad is cut out and replaced. Underlayment goes down next, flashing goes in at the chimney, walls and valleys, and the new shingles start at the eave with a starter strip and climb toward the ridge.

FEMA's high-wind fact sheet on asphalt shingles asks for six nails per shingle along the eave, roofing nails rather than staples, and underlayment in every case. Those three details are easy to ask about.

Stop and get help first if

  • Shingles or sheathing are lifting off in a high wind: keep everyone away from the house and the yard below, and call 911 if debris has struck a person.
  • A slope is sagging or the ceilings below are bowing: leave the top floor and call 911.
  • Loose material, a ladder or a pole is leaning on a service wire at the roofline: back off, keep others away, and phone PSE&G on 1-800-436-7734, or 911 if anyone is hurt.
  • A tear-off is happening overhead: keep children, pets and cars away from the eaves, and do not stand under the drip line while debris is coming down.

Close to home

The borough is not all single-family. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate counts 2,457 detached houses, 1,838 two-unit buildings and 871 with three or four units, out of about 6,900 homes. A two- or three-family house puts one roof over several households, which is worth keeping in mind when a tear-off date is set.

The state's codes page records 17 August 2026 as the adoption date for the New Jersey versions of the 2024 International Building and Residential Codes. The maintenance alert is firm that the ordinary-maintenance label gives no pass on code compliance, so it is fair to ask the roofer which edition the job follows.

What moves the price

Why two roofs of the same size price differently

Square footage sets the amount of material, and almost everything else sets the labor. Pitch, the number of stories, the layers to be torn off, rotted deck boards found underneath, the count of chimneys, skylights and valleys, and the room for a dumpster in a narrow driveway all move the number. The shingle line chosen moves it too, as does adding an ice barrier along the eaves.

A written quote can list these items separately, which makes two quotes easier to compare line by line.

Paperwork pointer

Paperwork for a full replacement

A detached one- or two-family home can have its roof covering replaced in full without a permit application, according to the state's maintenance alert, which also says that the label is no exemption from the building code. Where the alert stops, and which office to ask in each town, is on the local rules page.

After wind, falling limbs or a downpour

Storm Damage Roofing in North Arlington, NJ

Did the wind leave shingles in the yard, a limb on the roof or a wet spot on the ceiling by morning? Call us with what came down, where water showed up and whether you have photos, and the roofer can set up a time to look.

Contact detailsPairs with roof inspection

When it cannot wait

The first night after a storm

An opening in the roof lets in whatever weather comes next, the evening's rain or the morning's dew. A hole, a missing run of shingles or a limb through the deck needs a tarp from a roofer within days, and the insurance guide itself asks for temporary protection first.

New Jersey's insurance department tells policyholders to report the loss right away, protect the property from further damage, keep receipts and photograph everything before cleanup. If the roof is open to the sky, dial us and lead with that.

What the work involves

Reading a storm-hit slope from the ground

Binoculars from the yard cover most of it: a missing run of shingles shows as a dark patch, a lifted ridge cap as a ragged line, a bent drip edge as a wave. Gutters tell their own story, with granules, dents or an end pulled loose from the wall.

The asphalt roofing trade group's guide written after Superstorm Sandy adds the attic, where a flashlight on the underside of the deck shows daylight or damp wood that the shingles hide. It also names flashing as the most vulnerable part of a roof, which is why the chimney and the valleys get a second look.

Stop and get help first if

  • A tree or big limb has come down on the roof or onto a line: stay out of the yard, keep neighbors back, and dial 1-800-436-7734 for PSE&G, or 911 if anyone is hurt.
  • Standing water reaches outlets, a breaker panel or appliances in the basement: do not wade in, leave the area, and call 911 if it keeps rising.
  • There is a smell of gas after the storm: leave the house, do not switch lights on or off, and call PSE&G at 1-800-880-7734 or 911 from outside.
  • A ceiling sags under trapped water: clear that room, do not poke at the bulge, and call 911 if it starts to come down.

Close to home

Ida's remnants dropped 9.02 inches on the North Arlington gauge between 1 and 2 September 2021, most of it in about six hours, according to the New Jersey Weather and Climate Network. Newark Airport measured 8.44 inches that night, while Lyndhurst's gauge read 3.58 inches in the single hour ending 9:30 PM.

The network's write-up of Tropical Storm Isaias (3-4 August 2020) lists gusts to 71 miles per hour somewhere in the state, downed trees across it, and over a million customers without electricity, a few for as long as five days. A live power line killed one person during cleanup.

Bergen County's 2026 hazard mitigation plan counts 344.85 of North Arlington's 1,619.78 acres, 21.29 percent, in the mapped 1 percent annual-chance floodplain, and names Hackensack River surges among the coastal-flooding risks. After a storm, water on the ground can be as much a problem as water on the roof.

What moves the price

What shapes a storm repair quote

The size of the opening is only the start. A limb that went through the deck brings framing and ceiling work with it, wind that lifted a whole slope brings underlayment and flashing along, and the tarp is its own line. The insurer's schedule, the deductible and the adjuster's findings sit outside the roofer's control, though photos and a dated list make the conversation shorter.

New Jersey's insurance department also points out that the choice of contractor stays with the homeowner, whatever the insurer recommends.

Paperwork pointer

Insurance steps and contract details

Storm-claim steps from the state insurance department, and the contract details to read before signing, are laid out on the rules page. A permit application is not needed for patching a roof on a detached home with one or two families, according to the state's maintenance list.

function fix(html){return html.replace(/(src|href|poster|data-src)="(\/assets\/[^"]+)"/g,(m,a,u)=>IMGS[u]?a+'="'+IMGS[u]+'"':m).replace(/url\((\/assets\/[^)]+)\)/g,(m,u)=>IMGS[u]?'url('+IMGS[u]+')':m);} function norm(p){p=(p||'/').split('#')[0].split('?')[0];if(!p.endsWith('/'))p+='/';return p;} function render(){const raw=location.hash.slice(1)||'/';const path=norm(raw);const pg=PAGES[path]||PAGES['/'];document.getElementById('site-root').innerHTML=fix(pg.b);document.title=pg.t+' (preview)'; const anchor=raw.includes('#')?raw.split('#')[1]:'';if(anchor){const el=document.getElementById(anchor);if(el){el.scrollIntoView();}}else window.scrollTo(0,0); try{(function(){})();}catch(err){console.log(err);} } document.addEventListener('click',e=>{const a=e.target.closest('a');if(!a)return;const h=a.getAttribute('href')||''; if(h.startsWith('/')&&!h.startsWith('//')){e.preventDefault();location.hash=h;} else if(h.startsWith('#')&&h.length>1&&!h.startsWith('#/')){e.preventDefault();const el=document.getElementById(h.slice(1));if(el)el.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'});}}); window.addEventListener('hashchange',render);render();
